headline: Continued Beta Technologies' 101-acre master plan to 6 October 2026; withdrew Peregrine Design Build's 69 Randall Street site plan.
summary: The meeting continued the Beta Technologies master plan for a 101-acre area to 6 October 2026, after staff and the applicant discussed traffic, water lines, parking, and civic space. The Peregrine Design Build site plan for 69 Randall Street was withdrawn. The meeting also included a presentation on land development regulation amendments adopted 3 August 2026.
decisions: Withdrew Site Plan Application PZ-SITE-2026-11 for a 5040 sq. ft. building at 69 Randall Street.
Continued Beta Technologies master plan application PZ-MASTER-2026-2 to 6 October 2026; motion passed 5-0.

decision_evidence.quote: 6. Continued Site Plan Application #PZ-SITE-2026-11 of J. B. Development Corp., Inc., dba Peregrine Design Build, for anew 5040 sq. ft. footprint building on an existing undeveloped 3.05 acre lot, 69 Randall Street: Ms. Keene advised that this item was withdrawn.
Ms. Lesko then moved to continue PZ-MASTER-2026-2 until 6 October 2026. Mr. Kochman seconded. Motion passed 5-0.

decision_titles: Beta Technologies master plan for 101-acre area
plain_text:
PAGE 1 
MINUTES 
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 
15 SEPTEMBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington Development Review Board held a regular meeting on 
Tuesday, 15 September 2026, at 7:00 p.m. in the Auditorium, City Hall, 180 
Market Street, and via Go to Meeting interactive technology. 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: Q. Mann, Chair; M. Behr, F. Kochman, J. Lesko, C. Johnston 
 
ALSO PRESENT:  M. Keene, Development Review Planner; A. Levin, Planning 
Department; P. Conner, Director of Planning & Zoning; A. Gagnon, C. Gendron, K. 
Luce, M. J. Rizzo, D. Allen 
 
1. Instructions on exiting the building in case of an emergency:    
 
Ms. Mann provided instructions on emergency exit from the building. 
 
2. Additions, deletions, or changes in order of agenda items: 
 
No changes were made to the agenda. 
 
3. Comments and questions from the public not related to the Agenda: 
 
No issues were raised. 
 
4. Announcements: 
 
There were no announcements. 
 
5. Presentation on Amendments to the Land Development Regulations 
adopted 3 August 2026: 
 
Mr. Conner reviewed the amendments to the LDRs as follows:
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 2 
1. Nonconformities & Adaptive Reuse: Allows buildings that have existed 
for 15 years in districts that allow residential uses to be converted to a 
number of dwelling units.  Building square footage may be expanded by 
no more than 50%.   
       
     Aligns the definition of a non-conforming structure to City Center/Form 
Based Code; retains the status only if at least 50% of all load-bearing 
walls/pillar elements remain. 
 
    Updates allowance for expansion of non-conforming structures to be 50% 
of the square footage.  Allows greater expansion of historic buildings. 
 
Mr. Kochman asked if these are permitted or conditional uses.  Mr. Conner said 
they are permitted. 
 
2. Significant Natural Communities and RTEs:  Properties of 10 acres or 
more will be subject to study of rare/endangered species.  The Agency of 
Natural Resources (ANR) will get a copy of the application and can 
comment within 30 days.  No comment from ANR will be considered 
evidence that they are not raising a substantive issue. (The DRB should 
note this.)  The DRB may invoke technical review on elements of the 
application. 
 
Mr. Kochman stressed that this does not preclude the DRB from having an issue. 
 
3. Update to T4 Zoning: Expands Form Based Code to area including 
property north of Williston Road, west of I-89 in HSMU district. 
 
4. Use Updates: Data Center added as a defined commercial use and 
regulates size and location.  Also adds scales for Trucking Center 
Commercial uses and regulates their location.  
 
5. Minor technical amendments. 
 
6. Electric Vehicle Charging: re-establishes connection of City standards for 
EV charging to 2024 Residential Building Energy Standards and 2024 
Commercial Building Energy Standards.
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 3 
7. Zoning Permit Updates: Eliminates zoning permits for interior 
renovations and façade materials replacement or roof replacement as 
long as no expansion modifications or additional bedrooms. 
 
Mr. Conner then explained the T1A process to which municipalities with 
downtown village or growth areas are eligible.  There would be no longer an Act 
250 process in those areas.  The DRB has an important role in this.  If there is an 
application that already has an Act 250 permit, those permit conditions become 
part of the City permit if they are still relevant. 
 
Mr. Behr asked if there will be criteria for building conversions.  Mr. Conner said 
there will be standards, and all the other site plan criteria come into play. 
  
6. Continued Site Plan Application #PZ-SITE-2026-11 of J. B. Development 
Corp., Inc., dba Peregrine Design Build, for anew 5040 sq. ft. footprint 
building on an existing undeveloped 3.05 acre lot, 69 Randall Street: 
 
Ms. Keene advised that this item was withdrawn. 
 
7. Continued Master Plan Application #PZ-MASTER-2026-2 of Beta 
Technologies, Inc., to establish a master plan for a 101-acre area, 
consisting of 3 development areas including the previously approved 
Beta Master Plan area plus newly acquired properties in immediate 
proximity to the north and south of Williston Road: 
 
Staff comments were addressed as follows (picking up from where review left off 
at the previous hearing): 
 
 #13. Regarding the Traffic Impact Study, Ms. Mann asked if the applicant 
has an update.  Mr. Gendron said they have met with staff, and VTrans (who are 
totally on board with this).  The applicant’s responsibility will be to pull together 
the mitigation strategies.  The hope is to have something to review at the next 
hearing. 
 
 #14. Regarding additional traffic, Ms. Keene noted there will be an update 
with every application. 
 
 #15. (addressed at the previous meeting).  The applicant had nothing new 
to add.
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 4 
 
 #16. Regarding comments from the Director of Public Works about the 
water line.  Mr. Gendron said they are meeting with the Water Department 
tomorrow.  Their connection to Green Tree Drive is good. 
 
 #17. The applicant was asked to clarify whether there is distributed parking 
plan.  Mr. Gagnon said it is generally distributed, but there will be shuttles coming 
in from different locations.  Having parking distributed makes sense as it is a large 
campus with a lot of ground to cover.  Mr. Gendron added that they have 
identified a parking lot in Area 1. 
 
 #18. Staff feels the proposal to be on track but recommends that the DRB 
require the applicant to locate the civic space in Area 3 into the transition area and 
deconcentrate the scale and level of proposed commercial activity in a sensitive 
residential area.  Mr. Gendron said they will dedicate a portion of that area to civic 
space.  Mr. Gagnon added there will be a smooth transition from the residential 
area. 
Mr. Keene said she does not see anything about the scale/level of commercial 
activity.  Mr. Gendron said they can deal with noise, etc.  Ms. Mann asked that the 
applicant identify the type of commercial activity.  Mr. Gendron said they can do 
that. 
 
Mr. Behr asked if the applicant has scheduled another neighborhood meeting.  
Mr. Gagnon said it will be next week.  Information has been mailed. 
 
 #19. Staff asked that the applicant be required to provide information 
regarding roadway length, right-of-way, network characteristics, etc.  Mr. Behr 
said the Board will need a lot more detail as what is provided is still very 
preliminary. 
 
 #20. The applicant removed this request. 
 
 #21. Staff recommended the Board require satisfactory proposal triggers for 
civic space prior to closing the Master Plan.  Ms. Keene noted that the Board has 
allowed 2 separate applications, but they would not allow any zoning permit to be 
pulled until there is specific civic space approval.  Mr. Kochman stressed this has 
to be 10% usable civic space.  Ms. Mann suggested that civic space could be tied 
to a CO.  Mr. Gagnon said that makes more sense as people going into the 
building will be using the civic space.  Ms. Keene suggested there should be a CO 
for the civic space prior to the zoning permit CO.
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 5 
 
 #22. Regarding water line improvement triggers, Mr. Gendron said they are 
working with the Water Department on this, trying to iron out “grey areas.” 
 
 #23. The stormwater area has been shown. 
 
 #24. Regarding staging and temporary uses, staff asked the access roads, 
location of field offices, etc., be shown for each temporary use.  Ms. Keene 
stressed the need for clarity here.  Mr. Gendron said each site could be different; 
for a bigger project, there could be a bigger field office.  Ms. Keene said if there is 
equipment for one project on another site, that is a problem.  Mr. Kochman said 
there should be a condition so the City knows where everything is, and staff 
should be notified if things are being moved around. 
 
 #25. Regarding management responsibility, staff recommends the applicant 
disclose any change of the responsible party and delegate any future entities to 
comply with master plan commitments.  Ms. Gendron said that makes sense. 
 #26. Staff suggested the applicant be required to propose a framework for 
evaluation of whether improvements should be proposed for public dedication.  
Mr. Kochman asked why the Board should care at this point.  Mr. Behr said if they 
are building something to dedicate to the City, it should be built to City standards.  
Mr. Kochman said everything should be built to City standards.  Mr. Gendron said 
they will provide a framework for the next review. 
 
Mr. Johnston said they should talk about triggers at the next hearing (i.e., what 
might be outside the applicant’s control such as floods, supply chain, etc.).  
 
Public comment was then solicited and received as follows: 
 
Mr. Allen: He is a tenant at 3060 Williston Road and is seeking guidance regarding 
the future of the building.  Other tenants share the concern about a timeline or 
general strategy.  He noted the City of Burlington is now clearing out boxes and 
shredding contents.  Mr. Gendron said he can’t speak to timelines yet. He invited 
the tenants to the Wednesday meeting.  He stressed they are still developing a 
plan for the site.  Mr. Allen noted that one night power went out for an extended 
period of time with no warning which disrupted work of 2 of the tenants.  They 
would like a warning if this is to happen again.  Mr. Gendron note this property is 
in development area 2.  As it will be in the master plan, whatever happens should 
happen within 10 years.
DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 6 
Ms. Lesko then moved to continue PZ-MASTER-2026-2 until 6 October 2026.  Mr. 
Kochman seconded.  Motion passed 5-0. 
 
8.  Minutes: 
 
No minutes were reviewed.  
 
9. Other Business: 
 
No other business was presented. 
 
As there was no further business to come before the Board, the meeting was 
adjourned by common consent at 8:31 p.m. 
 
 
 
These minutes were approved by common consent on October 6, 2026.
